chunks.title: Field Shift Reviewed Agronomy & Scoring Guidance (EN/FR/AR)
chunks.section: 1.1 Why 3 Years is the Default Baseline (rotation_length: 3)
chunks.text:
In semi-arid Mediterranean rainfed systems (Sétif `regionA`), continental Great Plains rainfed systems (Central Kansas `regionB`), and irrigated Indo-Gangetic plains (Punjab `regionC`), a **3-year rotation horizon (`rotation_length = 3`)** is the shortest cycle that simultaneously satisfies three agronomic rules:
1. **Break cereal monoculture disease carryover** (`forbid_consecutive_same_family: true`): Take-all (*Gaeumannomyces graminis*), *Fusarium* crown rot, and grassy weeds (*Bromus*, *Phalaris minor*, jointed goatgrass) build up when two cereals follow each other.
2. **Respect the 2-year pulse disease break** (`max_occurrences_per_crop: 1`): Large-seeded legumes such as chickpea (*Ascochyta* blight), lentil (*Fusarium* wilt), and faba bean (*Orobanche* broomrape) require at least 2 years between identical pulse crops.
3. **Deliver a three-functional-group sequence**: Cereal (Year 1) → Nitrogen-Fixing Legume (Year 2, providing `-25%` synthetic NPK credit in Year 3) → Broadleaf Oilseed, Forage, or Alternate Cereal (Year 3).

chunks.title: Field Shift Reviewed Agronomy & Scoring Guidance (EN/FR/AR)
chunks.section: 1.2 Other Possible Rotation Periods (2-Year, 4-Year, 5-Year & Double-Cropping Seasons)
chunks.text:
The Python scoring engine (`engine/scoring.py`) is parameterized by `rules["rotation_length"]` in `domain/regions/<region>/rules.json` and evaluates `itertools.product(sorted(crops), repeat=rules["rotation_length"])`:
- **2-Year Period (`rotation_length = 2`, Cereal–Legume Biculture)**: Common in dryland Wheat–Lentil (Algeria), Corn–Soybean (Kansas), or Wheat–Mung bean. Pros: simple management, 50% legume frequency. Cons: a 1-year break is too short for *Ascochyta* blight in chickpea or *Aphanomyces* root rot in field pea, and leaves no slot for a deep-rooted oilseed taproot (canola, safflower, sunflower).
- **4-Year Period (`rotation_length = 4`, Cereal → Legume → Cereal → Oilseed/Forage)**: Ideal for diversifying weed control and allowing a full 3-year break before repeating sensitive pulses or brassicas (canola, mustard). Requires setting `max_occurrences_per_crop: 1` (with 4 distinct crops) or `2` (allowing wheat twice if separated by a legume and an oilseed).
- **5-Year Ley Rotation (`rotation_length = 5`, Perennial Alfalfa / Sulla Phase)**: Perennial forage legumes (`alfalfa` in Kansas, `sulla` in Sétif) occupy a field for 2 to 3 consecutive years to rebuild deep soil organic carbon (`soc_g_per_kg`) and fix `+30 to +45 kg N/ha/yr`, followed by 2 to 3 years of grain and oilseed cash crops.
- **Sub-Annual Double Cropping (2 Seasons/Year — Kharif + Rabi)**: In irrigated Punjab (`regionC`), farmers grow two crops per year (e.g., Kharif rice or maize in June–October followed by Rabi wheat, chickpea, or mustard in November–April), and sometimes a 65-day summer `mung_bean` catch crop in April–June. As disclosed in `G10`, the current engine models one primary crop per step; double-cropping sequences can be represented by pairing Kharif and Rabi crops across consecutive steps.

chunks.title: Field Shift Reviewed Agronomy & Scoring Guidance (EN/FR/AR)
chunks.section: 1.3 Résumé en Français (Durée de rotation : 2, 3, 4 ou 5 ans)
chunks.text: Le cycle de **3 ans (`rotation_length = 3`)** est la période minimale pour combiner une céréale, une légumineuse fixatrice d'azote (`nitrogen_fixing = 1`, réduisant l'engrais NPK de `-25%` l'année suivante) et un oléagineux ou fourrage, tout en évitant le retour trop rapide de l'anthracnose du pois chiche (*Ascochyta*) ou de l'orobanche. Le moteur Python (`engine/scoring.py`) accepte d'autres périodes via `rotation_length` dans `rules.json` : **2 ans** (blé–lentille ou maïs–soja), **4 ans** (céréale → légumineuse → céréale → colza/tournesol) ou **5 ans** (avec luzerne `alfalfa` ou sainfoin `sulla`).

chunks.title: Field Shift Reviewed Agronomy & Scoring Guidance (EN/FR/AR)
chunks.section: 1.4 ملخص بالعربية (فترة الدورة الزراعية: سنتان، 3 سنوات، 4 أو 5 سنوات)
chunks.text:
تُعد **الدورة الثلاثية (3 سنوات `rotation_length = 3`)** الفترة النموذجية لأنها تكسر أمراض الحبوب المتتالية (`forbid_consecutive_same_family`) وتمنح فترة راحة كافية للبقوليات ضد الأمراض الفطرية (مثل لفحة الأسكوكيتا في الحمص والهالوك في الفول)، مع توفير رصيد نيتروجين طبيعي يقلل السماد الكيميائي (`NPK`) بنسبة **25%** للمحصول التالي. يدعم محرك التقييم (`engine/scoring.py`) تغيير طول الدورة (`rotation_length`) إلى **سنتين** (قمح–عدس أو ذرة–صويا)، أو **4 سنوات** (حبوب ← بقوليات ← حبوب ← محاصيل زيتية مثل الكانولا والقرطم)، أو **5 سنوات** للمحاصيل العلفية المعمرة مثل الفصة (`alfalfa`) والسلة (`sulla`).

chunks.title: Field Shift Reviewed Agronomy & Scoring Guidance (EN/FR/AR)
chunks.section: 2.1 Four Criterion Scores (criterion_scores)
chunks.text:
For any candidate rotation $R = (c_1, c_2, \dots, c_n)$ of length $n$, `criterion_scores(rotation, crops)` computes four normalized scores in $[0, 1]$ (displayed as $0\text{–}100\%$ in the UI):
- **`profit` (`criteria.profit`)**: Mean of crop `profit` ratings across the rotation: $\text{mean}(\text{profit})$. Expected gross revenue is computed in `gross_income_dzd_ha` from regional `yield_potential` (q/ha) $\times$ `price_local`.
- **`water` (`criteria.water`)**: Water-saving score: $1 - \text{mean}(\text{water\_need})$. Lower crop `water_need` yields a higher `water` score. UI `waterNeed` is $(1 - \text{criteria.water}) \times 100$.
- **`soil` (`criteria.soil`)**: Soil protection & regeneration score: $0.5 \times \text{mean}(\text{residue\_carbon}) + 0.5 \times \min(1.0, 2 \times \text{mean}(\text{nitrogen\_fixing}))$. Rewards both crop residue carbon return and nitrogen-fixing legumes.
- **`risk` (`criteria.risk`)**: Risk safety score: $1 - \text{mean}(\text{risk\_level})$. Lower crop `risk_level` yields a higher `risk` score.

chunks.title: Field Shift Reviewed Agronomy & Scoring Guidance (EN/FR/AR)
chunks.section: 2.2 Climate & Soil Stress Weight Adjustment (derive_stress & adjust_weights)
chunks.text:
The engine reads local satellite indicators from `indicators.json` and `thresholds.json`:
- **`water_stress` (`stress.water_stress`)**: $\text{clamp}((\text{rainfall\_reference\_mm} - \text{rainfall\_mm}) / \text{rainfall\_reference\_mm}, 0, 1)$.
- **`soc_deficit` (`stress.soc_deficit`)**: $\text{clamp}((\text{soc\_threshold\_g\_per\_kg} - \text{soil\_organic\_carbon\_g\_per\_kg}) / \text{soc\_threshold\_g\_per\_kg}, 0, 1)$.
- **Dynamic weight amplification (`adjust_weights`)**:
  - $w_{\text{water}}' = w_{\text{water}} \times (1 + K_{\text{WATER}} \times \text{water\_stress})$ with $K_{\text{WATER}} = 1.0$.
  - $w_{\text{soil}}' = w_{\text{soil}} \times (1 + K_{\text{SOIL}} \times \text{soc\_deficit})$ with $K_{\text{SOIL}} = 1.0$.
  - All four weights (`profit`, `water`, `soil`, `risk`) are re-normalized to sum to $1.0$ in `adjusted_weights`, and `score = total_score(criteria, adjusted_weights)`.

chunks.title: Field Shift Reviewed Agronomy & Scoring Guidance (EN/FR/AR)
chunks.section: 2.3 Hybrid ML Transition Score, Environmental Match & 3-Year Soil Trajectory
chunks.text:
- **`env_match_pct` (`ml_metrics.env_match_pct`, UI "Climate match" / `scores.knn`)**: Checks whether regional `rainfall_mm` falls inside each crop's optimal rainfall envelope `[optimal_rain_min, optimal_rain_max]` (92% inside, Gaussian decay outside).
- **`ai_confidence_pct` (`ml_metrics.ai_confidence_pct`, UI "Crop sequence fit" / `scores.ml`)**: Pairwise transition probability rewarding family breaks (`family_break = +1.0` vs `-0.8` same family), legume nitrogen restoration after heavy feeders (`depletion >= 3` followed by `nitrogen_fixing == 1`), drought tolerance, and low water need.
- **`trajectory_3yr` (`simulate_3yr_trajectory`)**: Tracks year-by-year `projected_nitrogen_kg_ha` (starting from $45 + 2.5 \times \text{SOC}$), `soil_health_pct`, and `npk_dose_kg_ha`. When a crop follows a nitrogen-fixing legume (`legume_credit_applied: true`), its synthetic fertilizer dose `base_npk_kg_ha` is reduced by **25%** (`0.75 * base_npk`), yielding `total_3yr_npk_kg_ha` and `fertilizer_saved_vs_existing_kg_ha`.
- **`ranking_stability_pct` (`compute_ranking_stability`)**: Runs 100 seeded Monte Carlo weather simulations perturbing rainfall by $\pm 15\%$ and reports the percentage of years where Rank 1 stays on top.

chunks.section: Section 3: Scope Boundaries & What This Guidance Does NOT Cover (Refusal Policy)
chunks.text:
Field Shift's reviewed agronomy corpus covers **only**:
1. Multi-year crop rotation planning, agronomic rules (`rules.json`), and crop compatibility in `regionA` (Sétif, Algeria), `regionB` (Central Kansas, USA), and `regionC` (Punjab, India).
2. Engine scores (`score`, `criteria`, `adjusted_weights`, `stress`, `ml_metrics`, `trajectory_3yr`, `ranking_stability_pct`) and crop traits in `domain/crops_base.csv` and `domain/regions/*/yield.csv`.
3. Satellite climate, soil, NDVI, and Fire Watch indicators (NASA POWER, ERA5, ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0, MODIS MOD13Q1, NASA FIRMS VIIRS) and scientific disclosures `G1`–`G12`.

chunks.title: Field Shift Reviewed Agronomy & Scoring Guidance (EN/FR/AR)
chunks.section: Section 3: Scope Boundaries & What This Guidance Does NOT Cover (Refusal Policy)
chunks.text:
**Out-of-Scope Topics (Must Refuse):**
- Synthetic pesticide, herbicide, or fungicide brand prescriptions, spray mixing rates, or chemical pest eradication schedules.
- Livestock veterinary medicine, animal surgery, or feedlot antibiotic dosing.
- Tractor mechanics, combine harvester engine diagnostics, or IoT hardware wiring.
- Financial/cryptocurrency speculation, stock trading, legal land disputes, or non-agricultural topics.
- Tropical plantation crops not in the reviewed database (e.g., cocoa, coffee, oil palm, bananas, rubber).

chunks.title: Farmer's Guide: Choosing Your 3-Year Crop Plan
chunks.section: 🌱 Farmer's Guide: Choosing Your 3-Year Crop Plan
chunks.text:
Welcome! You do **not** need any computer skills to use this tool. If you can tap buttons on a phone or point with a mouse, you can finish your 3-year crop rotation plan in **3 minutes**.

> **What is this tool?** Think of it as a farming notebook that already knows your region's rainfall history, heat waves, and soil tiredness—and helps you pick which 3 crops to plant over the next 3 years so your land stays fertile and your harvest stays steady.

---

chunks.title: Farmer's Guide: Choosing Your 3-Year Crop Plan
chunks.section: 1. How It Works in 5 Simple Steps
chunks.text:
1. **Pick Your Region & Crops (`1. Setup`):**
   - Tap your language (`العربية`, `FR`, or `EN`) at the top right.
   - Choose your region and tap **✨ Suggest for my region** so the sliders adjust automatically for your local water and soil conditions.
   - Select the 3 crops you usually plant in **Year 1**, **Year 2**, and **Year 3**.
   - Tick the crops you allow on your farm (at least **3 crops**, including **one grain/cereal** like wheat or barley and **one bean/legume** like chickpea, lentil, or faba bean).
2. **Check Local Rain & Heat (`2. Climate Changes`):**
   - See your area's yearly rain, hot days (`>35 °C`), frost days (`<0 °C`), heavy rain days, and longest dry spell.
   - Move the **What-If Sliders** (for example, `-20%` less rain and `+2 °C` warmer) to see how your crops hold up in a tough year.
3. **Read the Best 3-Year Plans (`3. Rotation Ranking`):**
   - See the top-ranked 3-year rotations scored out of **100**, with plain-language risk warnings for every crop.
   - Tap **🖨️ Print or save as PDF** to take a paper sheet to the field or co-op.
4. **Compare With Your Usual Plan (`4. Usual vs Rank 1`):**
   - See your current 3-year rotation side by side with Rank 1 on **Water Need**, **Soil Health**, **Harvest Stability**, and **Estimated Income per hectare**.
5. **Explore the Region Map (`5. Region Map`):**
   - Tap any region marker on the map and toggle the rainfall-trend overlay to see which zones are drying fastest.

chunks.title: Farmer's Guide: Choosing Your 3-Year Crop Plan
chunks.section: 2. Why You Can Trust This Tool
chunks.text:
- **Built on real farming rules:** It never puts two crops from the same family back to back (which builds up pests and root disease), and it always includes a legume to restore natural nitrogen in the soil.
- **Tested against bad weather:** When the screen says *"rank 1 stays first in 87% of runs"*, it means we tested that rotation across dozens of drier and hotter scenarios—and it still came out on top.
- **Respects your current rotation:** We never hide your usual plan. We score it fairly right next to our #1 recommendation so you can judge the difference yourself.
- **Honest about its limits:** Satellite soil and rain maps measure whole neighborhoods (`250 m` squares), not every stone in your field—so your own eyes and experience always come first.

chunks.section: 3. Regional Agronomic Rules (data/regional/rules_algeria.json)
chunks.text: Every rule in [rules_algeria.json](file:///Users/morsistoredz/NasaSpaceApps/data/regional/rules_algeria.json) is derived from **ICARDA** and **ITGC** Mediterranean dryland experiments:

chunks.title: Regional Agronomic Rules, Crop Profiles & Data Sources
chunks.section: 3. Regional Agronomic Rules (data/regional/rules_algeria.json)
chunks.text:
1. **No Repeated Crop (`max_occurrences_per_crop = 1`):** Prevents *Fusarium* crown rot, *Ascochyta* blight spores, and parasitic *Orobanche* (broomrape) accumulation across a 3-year cycle.
2. **No Consecutive Same Botanical Family (`forbid_consecutive_same_family = true`):** Breaks grass weed cycles (wild oats / *Avena sterilis*) and cereal-specific root diseases by separating cereals with broadleaf legumes or oilseeds.
3. **Mandatory Legume Nitrogen Reset (`min_legumes = 1`):** Guarantees biological nitrogen fixation (`+20` to `+32 kg N/ha`) and activates ICARDA's **`-30%` synthetic fertilizer carryover rule** (`post_legume_npk_multiplier = 0.70`) for the following cereal.
4. **High-Water Cap (`max_high_water_crops = 1`, `high_water_need_threshold = 0.65`):** Prevents planting water-demanding break crops (`sunflower` `600–1000 mm`) repeatedly in dry regions (`Sétif`, `Tiaret`).
5. **Deterministic Tie-Breaker (`Alaa's Plan`):** Equal-scoring rotations always prioritize **Legume in Year 1 first**, then **alphabetical order**, guaranteeing 100% reproducible rankings on every run.
6. **Note on 3-Year Cyclic Family Mixing:** Under strict cyclic rules (`Year 3 -> Year 1`), alternating families requires **1 Cereal + 1 Legume + 1 Oilseed Break Crop** (implemented in [mockup.html](file:///Users/morsistoredz/NasaSpaceApps/mockup.html), with an automatic 2-family `Cereal <-> Legume` fallback if the farmer disables all oilseeds).

chunks.title: Agronomy & ML Scoring Guide
chunks.section: Part 1: Agronomy & Satellite Glossary for Computer Scientists
chunks.text: Think of a farm field as a **stateful server with a battery (`Soil Nitrogen & Carbon`), a cooling/power budget (`Water/Rainfall`), and security vulnerabilities (`Pests & Root Diseases`)**. Every crop is a workload you schedule for 1 year.

chunks.title: Agronomy & ML Scoring Guide
chunks.section: 1.1 Satellite & Climate Terms (NASA Data)
chunks.text:
| Term | Plain Definition | CS / Systems Analogy | Range & Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **NDVI** (*Normalized Difference Vegetation Index*) | Satellite measure of how green and dense plant leaves are, computed from Near-Infrared (`NIR`) and Red light: $\text{NDVI} = \frac{\text{NIR} - \text{Red}}{\text{NIR} + \text{Red}}$. Healthy green leaves reflect `NIR` and absorb `Red`. | **Server CPU/Throughput Utilization** measured from outside via telemetry. High peak `NDVI` in spring means crops in that pixel grew vigorously. | `-1.0` to `+1.0` (`< 0.2` bare soil; `0.3–0.5` sparse crop; `0.6–0.85` dense healthy crop) |
| **Evapotranspiration (`ET0` / `ETc`)** | Simply put: **total water leaving the field into the air** each day. It combines **Evaporation (`E`)** (water drying straight out of warm soil, like a puddle drying in the sun) + **Transpiration (`T`)** (water the plant drinks through its roots and "sweats" out through its leaves to stay cool). **`ET0`** is the baseline daily water loss of standard short green grass in that weather (sun + heat + wind + dry air); **`ETc`** is your specific crop's need (`ETc = ET0 × Kc`), e.g. sunflower drinks much more than barley. | **Total System Power Draw / Battery Drain Rate.** Think of **Rainfall** as money deposited into your soil bank account, and **`ETc`** as daily cash withdrawals. Even if `380 mm` falls, high `ET` drains moisture before roots can use it. | `mm/day` or `mm/season` (`ETc`: `300–450 mm` barley, `350–500 mm` wheat, `600–1000 mm` sunflower) |
| **Water Stress Index** | `1 - (recent_avg_rainfall / reference_20yr_rainfall)`, floored at `0`: $\text{clamp}\!\left(\frac{\text{Rain}_{\text{ref}} - \text{Rain}}{\text{Rain}_{\text{ref}}},\, 0,\, 1\right)$. | **Memory/Resource Pressure (`0%` = plenty of RAM, `100%` = OOM throttling).** High water stress boosts the weight of low-thirst crops. | `0.0` (no stress) to `1.0` (severe drought stress) |
| **Hot Days (`>35 °C`)** | Annual count of days where maximum air temperature (`T2M_MAX`) exceeds `35 °C`. During spring **grain filling** (when wheat kernels fill with starch), `>35 °C` shuts down plant enzymes and shrivels the harvest. | **Thermal Throttling during a critical write operation.** | `days/year` |
| **Frost Days (`<0 °C`)** | Annual count of days where minimum air temperature (`T2M_MIN`) drops below freezing. Late spring frost kills delicate flowers on legumes (chickpea, lentil, faba bean). | **Sudden power brownout during boot.** | `days/year` |
| **Longest Dry Spell & `PRECTOTCORR`** | Maximum consecutive days with `< 1 mm` of rain (`PRECTOTCORR < 1.0`). **`PRECTOTCORR`** is the standard variable name from **NASA POWER** (*Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources*), representing **bias-corrected total daily precipitation** in `mm/day`. | **Longest network outage window** the crop's root buffer must survive without rain packets arriving. | `consecutive days` (`PRECTOTCORR` in `mm/day`) |
| **Mann-Kendall & Sen's Slope (`Trend Confidence`)** | Two statistical tests on 30-year climate series: Ordinary Least Squares (parametric line fit) vs. Mann-Kendall/Sen's Slope (non-parametric rank test robust to outliers). When both show `p < 0.05` with the same sign, we show `"both methods agree"`; otherwise `"no clear trend"`. | **Consensus check between two independent anomaly detectors** before firing an alert. (`p-value` = probability the trend appeared by random chance). | `mm/decade` + confidence label |

| **SOC** (*Soil Organic Carbon*) | Carbon stored in decaying plant roots, stubble, and microbes in the top `0–30 cm` of soil. Holds water like a sponge and feeds soil microbes. | **Disk Cache + UPS Battery Capacity.** Low `SOC` (`< 10 g/kg`) means rain runs off the surface instead of soaking in. | `g/kg` (`SoilGrids` reports `dg/kg`, so divide by `10`; `10 g/kg = 1%` carbon) |
| **SOM** (*Soil Organic Matter*) | Total organic matter in soil. Roughly $\text{SOM} \approx 1.724 \times \text{SOC}$ (the van Bemmelen factor). | **Total allocated storage** vs. raw payload (`SOC`). Never mix the two without converting. | `%` or `g/kg` |
| **250 m Soil Estimate** | A modelled spatial average for a `250 m × 250 m` grid cell from global machine learning (`SoilGrids`), **not** a physical lab measurement of one farmer's field. | **Cluster-level telemetry average**, not a single-container probe. Always disclose this in `gaps.json`! | `250 m` pixel |
| **N, P, K** (*Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium*) | The 3 macro-nutrients every plant consumes: **N** builds green leaves/protein, **P** builds roots/flowers/seeds, **K** regulates water and disease resistance. | **CPU (`N`), Disk I/O (`P`), and Network Bandwidth (`K`).** If any one hits zero, crop growth halts (*Liebig's Law of the Minimum*). | `kg/ha` (or `mg/kg`) |
| **Fertilizer Codes (`NPK 10:26:26`, `DAP`, `MOP`, `Urea`)** | Commercial bags of synthetic nutrients. `NPK 10:26:26` is `10% N, 26% P, 26% K`. `DAP` (Diammonium Phosphate) is `18% N, 46% P`. `MOP` is Potassium (`0:0:60`). `Urea` is concentrated Nitrogen (`46% N`). | **Paid cloud burst capacity.** Expensive in cash and energy; legumes reduce how much `Urea`/`NPK` a farmer must buy (`-30%` next season). | `kg/ha` applied |
| **Soil `pH` (`phh2o`)** | Acidity (`< 6.0`), neutrality (`6.5–7.5`), or alkalinity (`> 7.8`, common in North African calcareous soils). Extreme `pH` chemically locks up Phosphorus and iron so roots cannot absorb them. | **File permission / protocol mismatch:** the data (`P`) is on disk, but the process can't read it outside `pH 6.0–7.8`. | `3.0–10.0` (`SoilGrids` reports `pH × 10`, so `79 = pH 7.9`) |

| **Cereals (Grains)** | Grass-family crops grown for starch grain and straw. Provide dependable yield and high **residue carbon** (stubble), but consume soil nitrogen. | **Steady production worker nodes** that consume battery (`N`) but leave good logs/mulch (`residue_carbon`). | Durum wheat, barley, oats |
| **Legumes (Pulses)** | Bean/pea-family crops whose roots host *Rhizobium* bacteria inside nodules that pull Nitrogen gas ($N_2$) from the air and turn it into natural soil fertilizer (`+20` to `+40 kg N/ha`). | **Solar charger / garbage collector** that recharges the soil `N` battery for next year's cereal crop. | Chickpea, lentil, faba bean |
| **Oilseeds (Break Crops)** | Broadleaf crops pressed for oil (`sunflower`, `rapeseed/canola`). Deep taproots break compacted soil layers and interrupt cereal root diseases. | **Cache flush & disk defragmenter** between cereal runs. | Rapeseed (canola), sunflower |

chunks.title: Agronomy & ML Scoring Guide
chunks.section: 2.1 Dataset 1 — NASA POWER Agro-Climatology (indicators.json)
chunks.text:
- **What it is:** Free global daily meteorology on a `0.5° × 0.625°` grid from NASA Langley Research Center (no API key needed).
- **Exact API URL (example for Setif `36.19°N, 5.41°E`):**
  `https://power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/daily/point?parameters=PRECTOTCORR,T2M_MAX,T2M_MIN,RH2M,EVPTRNS&community=AG&longitude=5.41&latitude=36.19&start=19950101&end=20241231&format=JSON`
- **Important Data Gotcha (CS View):** Missing values are encoded as **`-999`**. Always filter `val != -999` before computing means/counts, or your averages will corrupt!
- **How we process and use every field in code:**
  - `PRECTOTCORR` (`mm/day`): Sum per year $\rightarrow$ 30-year mean `rainfall_mm`; bin by month $\rightarrow$ `monthly_rain_mm` (12-bar chart on Screen 2); fit OLS + Mann-Kendall/Sen's slope $\rightarrow$ `rainfall_trend_decade_mm` & `trend_confidence`; compute `water_stress = clamp((rain_ref - rain_recent) / rain_ref, 0, 1)` which dynamically scales the Water weight (`1 + K_WATER * water_stress`).
  - `T2M_MAX` (`°C`): Count days `> 35 °C` $\rightarrow$ `hot_days` (triggers heat-stress warning on wheat grain filling).
  - `T2M_MIN` (`°C`): Count days `< 0 °C` $\rightarrow$ `frost_days` (triggers frost-risk warning on winter chickpea/lentil).
  - `PRECTOTCORR > 20 mm`: Count $\rightarrow$ `extreme_rain_days`; consecutive `< 1 mm` $\rightarrow$ `longest_dry_spell_days`.

chunks.title: Agronomy & ML Scoring Guide
chunks.section: 2.2 Dataset 2 — NASA MODIS MOD13Q1 Vegetation Index (indicators.json)
chunks.text:
- **What it is:** 16-day composite satellite greenness (`250 m` resolution) via **NASA AppEEARS** (`https://appeears.earthdatacloud.nasa.gov/`) or Google Earth Engine (`MODIS/061/MOD13Q1`).
- **Important Data Gotcha (CS View):** `NDVI` in raw MODIS GeoTIFF/HDF files is stored as an integer scaled by **`10000`** (`5400` = `0.54`). Also, you **must mask pixels** with **ESA WorldCover `class 40` (Cropland)** so forests, buildings, and bare rock do not pollute the farm signal.
- **How we use it in code:**
  - Extract spring peak `NDVI` (`March–May` in North Africa) for each year.
  - Normalize regional mean peak `NDVI` (`0.25–0.75` $\rightarrow$ `0.0–1.0`) as `yield_baseline` in `indicators.json` (used to contextualize regional productivity, never claimed as a parcel-level yield forecast).
  - Compute Coefficient of Variation ($CV = \sigma / \mu$) across years as historical biomass instability.

chunks.title: Agronomy & ML Scoring Guide
chunks.section: 2.3 Dataset 3 — ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 (soil.json $\rightarrow$ indicators.json)
chunks.text:
- **What it is:** Global `250 m` digital soil map via REST API (`https://rest.isric.org/soilgrids/v2.0/properties/query`), implemented in [scripts/fetch_soilgrids.py](file:///Users/morsistoredz/NasaSpaceApps/scripts/fetch_soilgrids.py).
- **Properties to pull (`0-5cm`, `5-15cm`, `15-30cm`):**
  - `soc`: Soil Organic Carbon in `dg/kg` $\rightarrow$ **divide by `10`** to get `g/kg`.
  - `phh2o`: Soil pH in `pH × 10` $\rightarrow$ **divide by `10`** to get `pH`.
  - `nitrogen`: Total nitrogen (`cg/kg`) for soil baseline context (note: **not** plant-available mineral NPK).
- **How we process and use it in code:**
  - Compute the `0–30 cm` depth-weighted mean using layer thicknesses `5 : 10 : 15` (`total = 30 cm`):
    $$\text{SOC}_{0\text{–}30} = \frac{5 \cdot \text{L}_{0\text{–}5} + 10 \cdot \text{L}_{5\text{–}15} + 15 \cdot \text{L}_{15\text{–}30}}{30} \div 10$$
  - Map `soc_g_kg` to `soil_stress` (`low SOC < 10 g/kg` $\rightarrow$ `1.0`; `medium 10–20` $\rightarrow$ `0.5`; `high > 20` $\rightarrow$ `0.0`), which scales the Soil weight (`1 + K_SOIL * soil_stress`) and sets the starting `Soil Health %` in the 3-year trajectory simulator.

chunks.title: Agronomy & ML Scoring Guide
chunks.section: 2.4 Dataset 4 — Regional Crop Table & Agronomic Rules (crops.csv & rules.json)
chunks.text:
- **Where to source for Algeria / Mediterranean (instead of `CropSense`'s 22 Indian crops):**
  1. **FAOSTAT (`https://www.fao.org/faostat/`):** Top regional cereals (`durum wheat`, `barley`, `oats`) and legumes (`chickpea`, `lentil`, `faba bean`) + national/regional yield benchmarks.
  2. **FAO EcoCrop (`https://gaez.fao.org/` / EcoCrop DB):** Optimal temperature, rainfall (`mm`), and `pH` envelopes for each Mediterranean crop (replaces `CropSense`'s tropical `Crop_recommendation.csv` envelopes).
  3. **Local Extension Sheets (ITGC Algeria / ICARDA):** Agronomic rules (`min_legumes_in_3_years = 1`, `max_cereals_in_3_years = 2`, no consecutive same-crop/same-family) and crop-specific `risk_note` strings (`"needs local review"`).
- **Schema (`data/inputs/crops.csv`):**
  `crop, family, water_need, nitrogen_fixing, residue_carbon, drought_tolerance, profit, risk_level, soil_depletion_index, nitrogen_impact_kg_ha, soil_health_delta, base_npk_kg_ha, optimal_rain_min, optimal_rain_max, optimal_ph_min, optimal_ph_max, risk_note`
- **How we use it in code:**
  - `rules.json` filters the `n^3` combinations (`4^3 = 64` $\rightarrow$ `24` legal rotations) in **Stage 1** before any scoring happens, and populates the **"🚫 Rotations & Crops to Avoid"** panel.
  - `crops.csv` drives the marks (`water`, `soil`, `yield`), contextual tags (`🌿 Restores Nitrogen`, `💧 Low Water`), KNN environmental niche matching, and 3-year soil/NPK simulation.

chunks.title: Agronomy & ML Scoring Guide
chunks.section: 2.5 Dataset 5 — Data Limitations & Scenario Config (gaps.json)
chunks.text:
- **What it is:** Structured honesty metadata authored with `Nazim` & `Achref` (e.g., `"250 m SoilGrids cell is a regional average, not a single-field lab NPK test"`, `"NASA POWER 0.5° grid smooths local micro-valleys"`).
- **How we use it in code:** Every recommendation's `E5` explanation block pulls directly from `gaps.json` and `indicators.json` (zero hardcoded free text), ensuring transparent scientific communication for farmers and NASA judges.

---

chunks.title: Agronomy & ML Scoring Guide
chunks.section: Part 3: Upgrading the Engine from Pure Rules to Hybrid AI/ML
chunks.text:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Why Hybrid AI beats "Pure ML" or "Pure Rules" in Agronomy (and matches your Field Shift Rules):**
> - **Pure Rules** are 100% transparent and never recommend illegal rotations, but cannot score continuous climate-soil suitability or multi-year state dynamics.
> - **Pure ML** without domain rules will occasionally hallucinate an illegal rotation, and `CropSense`'s RF (`0.92`) only learned rule-generated labels.
> - **The Professional Hybrid Standard:** **Stage 1 Hard Rules** $\rightarrow$ **Stage 2 Environmental Niche Suitability (KNN-style distance)** $\rightarrow$ **Stage 3 Pairwise Transition Scoring** $\rightarrow$ **Stage 4 3-Year Soil & Fertilizer State Simulator** $\rightarrow$ **Stage 5 Stress-Adaptive Scoring & Monte Carlo Stability**.

    S2["Stage 2: Environmental Niche Match (KNN-style feature distance)\nMatches region rain/pH/SOC to crop optimal envelopes"] --> S3

chunks.title: Agronomy & ML Scoring Guide
chunks.section: Alignment with Your Team's Build Order (E1–E8)
chunks.text:
1. **`E1` Validation:** Verify all crop names match `crops.csv`, all metrics are in `[0, 100]`, and sliders are not all zero.
2. **`E2` Candidate Generation & Rules (`Stage 1`):** Generate all 3-year permutations (`product(allowed_crops, repeat=3)`), filter via `rules.json`, and record blocked rotations/crops for the UI warning list.
3. **`E3–E4` Marks, Stress-Adaptive Weights & Deterministic Tie-Breaker:**
   - Adjust slider weights by `(1 + K_WATER * water_stress)` and `(1 + K_SOIL * soil_stress)`, re-normalize to sum to `1.0`.
   - Group by `frozenset(rot)` (best order per distinct crop set), tie-break deterministically (**legume in Year 1 first, then alphabetical**), and always include the farmer's **Usual Rotation** (unfiltered) for comparison.
4. **`E5` Data-Driven Explanations + Contextual Tags:** Populate `why`, `evidence`, `benefits` (`🌿 Restores Nitrogen`, `💧 Low Water`, `☀️ Drought Tolerant`), `gaps` (from `gaps.json`), and `risks` (from `crops.csv` `risk_note`).
5. **`E6–E8` API, Tests & Monte Carlo Stability:** Expose JSON to FastAPI/HTML UI, verify against hand calculations in `logs/test_log.md`, and run `N=100+` rainfall perturbations (`±10–15%`) so `ranking_stability_pct` is **always computed live, never hardcoded**.

chunks.title: About the Data — Sources, Methods & Confidence Rules
chunks.section: NASA POWER (daily weather)
chunks.text:
- **What it is**: NASA Langley's "Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources" — satellite-derived, gridded meteorology; our source for daily rain (PRECTOTCORR), Tmax (T2M_MAX), Tmin (T2M_MIN), 1995–2024.
- **Resolution**: the underlying MERRA-2/SWCCCC grid is ~0.5° × 0.625° (≈50 km); POWER interpolates to the requested point, which does **not** add real detail. Daily meteorology available from 1981.
- **Known limits (observed here)**: systematically wetter than ERA5 by 13–43% over 1995–2024 in our three regions; ERA5 values sit inside the ITGC ranges, POWER's Constantine/Tiaret values sit above them. A gridded product, not a station measurement.
- **Attribution (verified at https://power.larc.nasa.gov/docs/referencing/)**: include both:
  - *Reference*: "The data was obtained from National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Langley Research Center's Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources (POWER) project funded through the NASA Earth Science Division."
  - *Data reference*: "The data was obtained from the POWER Project's Daily 2.x.x version on 2026-11-13." (adjust version/date to the actual fetch)
  - License: CC BY 4.0, no other restrictions (verified via registry.opendata.aws/nasa-power). POWER also requests a notification for published uses (larc-power-project@mail.nasa.gov) — flagged for Aniss if we publish.

chunks.title: About the Data — Sources, Methods & Confidence Rules
chunks.section: ISRIC SoilGrids (SOC, pH)
chunks.text:
- **What it is**: machine-learning global soil property maps from ~230,000 profile observations; our source for soil organic carbon and pH (0–30 cm).
- **Resolution**: 250 m model estimate with quantified uncertainty (we do not yet pull the uncertainty layers). It is a prediction, not a lab measurement of our plots.
- **Attribution (verified at https://docs.isric.org/globaldata/soilgrids/SoilGrids_faqs_04.html)**: license CC BY 4.0; cite as: Poggio, L., de Sousa, L. M., Batjes, N. H., Heuvelink, G. B. M., Kempen, B., Ribeiro, E., and Rossiter, D.: *SoilGrids 2.0: producing soil information for the globe with quantified spatial uncertainty*, SOIL, 7, 217–240, 2021. https://doi.org/10.5194/soil-7-217-2021 (DOI as printed in the FAQ).

chunks.title: About the Data — Sources, Methods & Confidence Rules
chunks.section: MODIS NDVI (MOD13Q1 via ORNL DAAC subsetting)
chunks.text:
- **What it is**: Terra MODIS 16-day vegetation indices at 250 m; we use NDVI spring peaks (DOY 65–145, 2020–2024) from the ORNL DAAC MODIS subsetting service around each region point.
- **Known limits (observed here)**: no cropland mask (the 5×5 km patch mixes field crops, roads, fallow), no per-pixel QA filtering in our pipeline, only 5 years, and the yield baseline (0.25–0.75 normalization) is a linear proxy — hence "low" confidence.
- **Attribution (verified via https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/news/lp-daac-releases-modis-version-61-vegetation-indices-data-products/ and earthdata.nasa.gov)**: Didan, K., 2021, MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 250m SIN Grid V061 [dataset], NASA Land Processes DAAC, https://doi.org/10.5067/MODIS/MOD13Q1.061. Accessed 2026-11-13. LP DAAC data has no restrictions on use (EOSDIS Data Use and Citation Guidance). Our access went through the ORNL DAAC subsetting tool — cite the product DOI above and mention the ORNL DAAC service by name.

chunks.text: Draft for Younes/Aniss to review and shorten as needed. Plain English; a French/Arabic version is a Should.

chunks.title: Glossary of Data & Agronomic Terms
chunks.section: NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index)
chunks.text: A greenness score from satellite pictures. Healthy, dense crops reflect more near-infrared light, which raises the score. Bare soil is around 0.1–0.2; a strong wheat canopy reaches 0.6–0.8. We use the spring peak NDVI near each region only as a rough proxy of how the vegetation has been doing — not a yield measurement.

chunks.title: Glossary of Data & Agronomic Terms
chunks.section: Evapotranspiration (ET)
chunks.text: The water a field "breathes out" — evaporation from the soil plus transpiration through the plants. Hot, dry, windy days push it up; when ET is much higher than rainfall, the crop is living on soil water. (Not yet an indicator in our pipeline — a Should.)

chunks.title: Glossary of Data & Agronomic Terms
chunks.section: Soil moisture anomaly
chunks.text: How much wetter or drier the soil is right now compared with its usual level for the same date, on the same spot. A strongly negative anomaly for weeks means the drought is real in the root zone, not just in the rain gauge. (Not yet in the pipeline; SMAP satellite data could give it.)

chunks.title: Glossary of Data & Agronomic Terms
chunks.section: Frost risk (as we measure it)
chunks.text: Not "it froze this winter", but "how often sub-zero nights fall *after* the crop starts growing". We count nights below 0 °C between 1 March and 30 April — the window when a frost can kill young wheat ears. The whole-winter count is a different, much larger number; don't mix them.

chunks.title: Glossary of Data & Agronomic Terms
chunks.section: Water stress (as we compute it)
chunks.text: How much drier recent years were than the region's own long-term average: `1 − (recent rainfall / 1995–2014 average)`. 0 means recent rainfall matches the old average; 0.2 means recent years were 20% drier. It compares a region with itself, so a measurement bias that affects both periods partially cancels.

chunks.title: Glossary of Data & Agronomic Terms
chunks.section: Trend confidence
chunks.text: Rainfall changes slowly and noisily, so we run two independent tests (least-squares slope and the rank-based Mann–Kendall test). Only when both agree the decline is real do we label "both methods agree" with high confidence. One test alone can be fooled by a few extreme years.

chunks.title: Glossary of Data & Agronomic Terms
chunks.section: 250 m soil estimate
chunks.text: The soil numbers (organic carbon, pH) are not from your field. SoilGrids is a computer model that blends thousands of lab-analyzed soil profiles with satellite data and predicts values everywhere on a 250 m grid. Treat it as regional background: good for comparing regions, not for deciding fertilizer on one plot. That's why its confidence is capped at "medium".

chunks.title: Glossary of Data & Agronomic Terms
chunks.section: Reanalysis vs station measurement
chunks.text: A weather station measures real rain at one point — accurate there, but rare here. A **reanalysis** (POWER, ERA5) takes millions of observations from satellites and a global weather model and reconstructs a complete, gap-free record on a ~25–50 km grid. Advantages: every point covered, every day since 1981+. Disadvantage: each grid cell is an average over a huge area — a storm that hit one village can be invisible, and mountains are smoothed out. We cross-check two independent reanalyses (NASA POWER vs ERA5) and show their disagreement as a confidence label.

chunks.title: Scientific Limitations & Scale Disclosures (G1–G12)
chunks.section: Scientific Disclosures G1 to G12
chunks.text:
- G1: Soil SOC and pH come from 250 m ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 modelled cells (0-30 cm), not a laboratory NPK soil test of your single parcel.
- G2: NASA POWER climate telemetry uses a 0.5° × 0.625° grid (~55 km), which smooths micro-valley rainfall and frost pockets.
- G3: MODIS MOD13Q1 spring peak NDVI (2020-2024, 5×5 km patch average) mixes cropland with roads and fallow; no cropland mask or pixel QA filter was applied.
- G4: Legume biological nitrogen fixation (+20 to +32 kg N/ha) is an ICARDA dryland benchmark; actual carryover depends on rhizobia nodulation and grazing management.
- G5: Gross income uses official OAIC/CCLS campaign prices (DA/q) × regional yield; net profit varies with fuel, seed, and CCLS quality grades (bonifications/réfractions).
- G6: NASA POWER shows 13-43% higher rainfall than Open-Meteo ERA5 reanalysis across the three regions; cross-check confidence labels reflect this spread.
- G7: Soil erosion risk cannot be estimated reliably from current inputs (RUSLE factors absent), so no numeric erosion claim is fabricated.
- G8: Water-stress magnitude depends on the recent comparison window (2015-2024 vs 2020-2024 sensitivity variant) while relative stress stays positive everywhere.
- G9: Water stress is computed from meteoric rainfall (NASA POWER). In irrigated regions such as the Punjab Plains (India) or irrigated pockets of the US Great Plains, canal and tube-well water mask rainfall deficits while depleting groundwater aquifers.
- G10: Many South Asian farms grow two crops per year (e.g. Kharif rice followed by Rabi wheat). Our engine models one primary crop per year across a 3-year sequence; multi-season double-cropping is documented as a future improvement.
- G11: Light regions (Central Kansas, USA and Punjab Plains, India) use public national datasets (USDA NASS, FAOSTAT, ICAR) without local field-trial calibration and are labeled 'Less validated'. NASA POWER grid cells (~50 km) represent flat regional farmland rather than individual parcels.
- G12: NASA FIRMS (VIIRS 375 m / MODIS 1 km) detects actively burning thermal anomalies (~3 hours latency). It is not a fire forecast or danger index; cloud cover or small fires can be missed, and industrial hotspots can appear.
